about.title: If your DevOps creates infrastructure by clicking, you do not have a DevOps engineer.
about.p1: I'm Max: a DevOps and platform engineer who believes everything that has an API should be configured as code. Since 2019 I have built and run clouds, Kubernetes clusters and delivery pipelines for startups, enterprises, an ad-tech private cloud of about 400 hosts and a government fraud-detection platform.
about.p2: Most of my employers were outsourcing companies, so I learned to land in an unfamiliar system, read it like an X-ray and make it boring: simple, documented, reproducible. My test for every decision is one question: how will this feel to maintain in two years?
about.p3: These days I also use AI-assisted coding to go end to end: from the Terraform module to the frontend that sits on top of it.

automation.title: I automate everything. Then I automate the automation.
automation.intro: A change I make travels the same road every time: commit, test, plan, apply, deploy, observe. No console clicks, no snowflake servers, no "it works on my laptop".
stepHints: git push to a protected branch
applied by CI through OIDC, no keys
GitOps: ArgoCD or Vercel ships it
manualLines: copy settings to staging by hand
nobody knows why prod is different
autoLines: review the diff in a pull request
CI applies it with short-lived credentials
staging and prod come from one module

items.text: Since March 2026 I launch and run my own small businesses, automated the same way I build platforms: sites, bookings and ads as code.
Built a greenfield platform after the acquisition: Terraform, EKS with GitOps through ArgoCD, secure CI/CD, on-call and incident response.
Owned AWS, Terraform and Terragrunt, Kubernetes and monitoring end to end; delivered multi-region; the startup was acquired by Mimecast.
A new client and a new toolset every three months: AWS and on-prem, greenfield and legacy.
A private cloud of about 400 bare-metal and virtual hosts in three regions; PXE provisioning, Terraform on vSphere, Kubernetes with Ansible.
Rebuilt monitoring and logging for a fraud-detection platform in a locked-down network; promoted after one month.
Where it started: LAMP sites and technical SEO, then on-call L1–L3 support for big-data platforms.
